  3. Baron Blade deals Baron Blade 3 damage.

xThe Killswitch:

Meh, still doesn't feel right to me.

My intuition is also that it doesn't feel right, but I have a way of looking at it that helps me, and perhaps it will help you.

 

For temporary reductions, it 'feels wrong' that they aren't used up in a redirection, because if you weren't reducing anything, how could you have redirected it? The real question to ask here, though, isn't 'Why aren't temporary reductions used before a redirection lost', but, rather, 'Why ARE continuing reductions lost?'

 

Imagine there is some effect reducing damage to Fixer down to two or less (perhaps Fixer would be dealt three damage but Argent Adept has chosen Fixer to have damage reduced by one). The only reason that Fixer can redirect this damage is because it would have been reduced, so if the damage is redirected, shouldn't it ACTUALLY be reduced? The literal reading of the cards (would have, as opposed to is/was reduced) argues against this, but logically it seems to me that either it is reduced and redirected or it couldn't be redirected.

 

Now, there is very well established precedent and rulings for how the game works, so I am NOT TRYING to start a discussion about changing how the game works. My point is that if you can accept that the damage isn't reduced for a continuing reduction effect, I think it's a relatively small step to accept that the damage isn't reduced for a one-time reduction effect.

 

PS I think it might be interesting to think through what a set of rules would look like in which a reduction required for a redirection was actually applied after the redirection, but I also know that Christopher et. al. put a lot of effort into creating a set of cards that work without undue complexity. I have heard about all of the complexity involved in understanding the precise order of what happens in MtG. I'm glad we don't have that.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
Let me make a few parallel arguments:

1.  Look at Twist the Ether, you reselect Twist the Ether entirely when it is redirected.  It isn't a new instance of damage, you already changed the type and increased or decreased it, but then when it gets redirected you cancel the initial application of Twist, as if it never happened and proceed to then use the effect.

That function makes no sense if on redirection the Twist effect still counts as having been used.  But you completely undo Twist's effect and re-apply.

To me that says that the effect would have taken place, but was cancelled before it resolved, and so had to start over.  Apply that to Stealth or a PW'd Haka of Shielding and it should work the same way, the amount is tentatively reduced, then redirected at which point the reduction doesn't resolve and isn't consumed.  The new target would recheck to see what effects can reduce or increase and find that Stealth/Shielding doesn't apply.

2.  Let's take DW Setback's ability and apply it to this same situation:

Damage being dealt to Fixer reduced by 2 and redirected, if Fixer targets a non-hero then it won't still be reduced.  If the redirection targets a hero target, would Setback's power still reduce the damage?  It should, because the reduction hasn't happened.  Yet we know that at the moment of redirection the reduction is undone and is re-checked, so only if the initial reduction didn't count as having resolved the reduction effect would it still be available to reduce the redirected damage.

I've done this before to trigger Cryo Bot.

With the way we now know Twist works on redirection and the DW Setback power I think redirection leaves a tentative reduction unresolved, and still "on the field."

There was an interaction I realized I wanted to try, that is similar but it is not redirection.

I had Haka become incapped (Awesomely the Mega Computer allows a heroes to start incapped, so that was easy), then I got into play Undaunted, later I eventually drew the card I needed, Divine Sacrifice. So after declaring that Fanatic would recieve a -2 from Haka, I played the Divine Sacrifice, since it is irreducible it could not be reduced, however it is one damage so it was prevented by Undaunted. I then had Fanatic Absolution herself for 3 damage, which it did get reduced to 1 and thus prevented. I then had LEgacy use Motivational Charge (boosted by 1 thanks to Surge of Strength) to deal 3 to Fanatic, it was not reduced.

The next round, I once again had Haka use his incap power to reduce the next damage Fanatic takes be 2 again. This time I played Concencrated Ground, dealing Fanatic 1 point of damage, then it was reduced by 2 and did not give the option to select Undaunted first. 

So it seems that if something that reduces the next damage a hero takes and that damage is irreducible and the hero is able to prevent it, the reduction is not used. If it succeeds in reducing damage and the hero has means to prevent the reduced damage, then the reduction is used. If the hero reduces the damage 0 or fewer, then prevention cannot trigger.

Of course this isn't redirection, so it's still a mystery how it will resolve, but it may help a bit knowing how it works with prevention.
